abstract: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a cognitive disorder associated with cerebrovascular pathology, but its molecular regulation remains incompletely understood. This study examined microRNA-208a-5p (miR-208a-5p) and its relationship with silent information regulator 1 (SIRT1). Bioinformatic analysis of GSE120584 identified hsa-miR-208a-5p as a candidate VaD-associated miRNA. Its expression was increased in a rat two-vessel occlusion (2VO) model and in primary cortical neurons exposed to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R), whereas SIRT1 expression was reduced. SIRT1 was identified as a common predicted target of miR-208a-5p. Dual-luciferase reporter assays supported binding of miR-208a-5p to the SIRT1 3'-untranslated region (3'-UTR). miR-208a-5p inhibition was associated with increased SIRT1 abundance, reduced apoptosis and oxidative stress, and preserved mitochondrial membrane potential in vitro. Early preventive hippocampal delivery of an adeno-associated virus (AAV)-miR-208a-5p sponge improved Morris water maze (MWM) performance and attenuated histological and biochemical abnormalities. These findings suggest that miR-208a-5p acts as a candidate regulator in VaD and that SIRT1 is a candidate direct target. Further rescue and loss-of-function studies are required to establish whether these effects are SIRT1-dependent.
